question: Which wastewater plants should Horton call first?
html:
Which plants Horton should call first

Horton should call New Haven East Shore, Hartford and Norwalk first. All three are Connecticut plants with work on the state's fundable list, and they lead both the target ranking and the growth plan. MWRA Deer Island and Bridgeport Westside come next (CET wastewater-plant targets; CET growth plan).

First-call list

RankPlantFitFundable workRequested work
1New Haven East Shore (40 MGD)98$82M wet-weather/odor control, FY27$19.2M process-air compressors
2Hartford WPCF (60 MGD)96$24.3M sludge screening/equalization, FY26-27$31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations
3Norwalk WPCF (18 MGD)95$26M final settling tanks, FY27$48M aeration system
4MWRA Deer Island (MA)94$289M Clarifier #2 in 2026 IUP—
5Bridgeport Westside (30 MGD)93Rationale truncated in dataset—

Sources: CET wastewater-plant targets.

Why this order

  • New Haven and Hartford are regional authorities with large design flows. Each has a fundable project and a second request behind it (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Norwalk offers the clearest pairing of Horton and NuWave. Aeration is the plant's biggest energy load, and a $48M green aeration request sits behind the funded tank job.
  • Deer Island already self-generates 26% of its power. The pitch there is electrical subcontracting plus storage and efficiency, not solar.
  • Bridgeport Westside shows 12 quarters with noncompliance and 1 with significant noncompliance. Its last inspection was 683 days ago, and its permit has been administratively continued since June 30, 2024 (EPA wastewater-plant compliance). Treat this as a signal of possible upcoming capital work, not as a funded project.

Caveats

  • Only Connecticut Table 2 / Category I items are fundable. The compressor, pump-station and aeration figures are Table 3 requests that compete for first-come reserves (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • The Rhode Island list is a June 2026 draft. Only its Table 2 items are proposed for funding.
  • The total pipeline value for New Haven is cut off in the dataset. Hartford's pipeline is about $105.7M and Norwalk's is $76.5M.
  • Win rates and Horton's share of each project are not in the context. Bid-history data from Horton would be needed to size the revenue (est. only if modelled).

Next actions

  • Map Horton's existing relationships at the Greater New Haven WPCA, the MDC and Norwalk. Name an owner for each call by Oct 16, 2026.
  • Pull the bid schedules and engineer-of-record contacts for the three funded Connecticut projects. Confirm the procurement timing.
  • Build a joint Horton/NuWave efficiency case for the Norwalk aeration request before it moves to the fundable list.
  • Recover the full Bridgeport Westside rationale and ranks 6-15 from the target file. Then decide whether Deer Island needs a separate MA subcontracting approach.
